items.line: Fox News reports that the FBI’s National Crime Information Center, a database used for background checks and for sharing warrant information among law enforcement agencies, has been hacked. The post says it is unclear what was taken. Not checked here.
Popstonox says Donald Trump shared Abdul El-Sayed's Medicare for All proposal on Truth Social, and that El-Sayed had suggested renaming it "TrumpCare for All". Not checked here.
Radec posts a 29-second video, credited to Reddit user MelloYello917, that he says shows the best way to get money in GTA 6. The post does not describe the video. Not checked here.
The account Nancy Pelosi Stock Tracker says a Senate vote to end the Iran war failed again, 48 to 51, and that Sen. John Fetterman was the lone Democrat blocking it. Not checked here.

Tesla says FSD v15 is starting to roll out, and lists a claim of 25x better handling of safety critical cases, a live visualization called Reality View, and slowing for speed cameras. Tesla's claims; not checked here.

The Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative say they have verified a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis that Levent Alpöge released on November 20 as a Lean library of 17 million lines of code. Not checked here.
PETA posts "Here’s an idea: don’t eat turkey for Thanksgiving this year."

Mario Nawfal posts that Iran says its Revolutionary Guard hit two US Patriot radars at bases in Bahrain, while Bahrain says a civilian industrial site burned. The post says the two accounts do not match. Not checked here.
Reuters reports that a town in southern Brazil has been left reeling by a supercell storm.
Osint613 reports that at least three people have died and 39 are missing after a fire at a candy factory in Serang, Indonesia, and that search and rescue is ongoing. Not checked here.
Nature Unedited posts an 87-second video and says a massive deep-sea shark was filmed approaching a submarine during an expedition. What the video shows is not checked here.
Elon Musk writes "It's high time we probed Uranus again! Much better images are needed (actually)."

Mario Nawfal says Trump told reporters on Friday that China's roughly 600 warheads will catch up with the American arsenal within 10 years. He adds retired Air Force general Rob Spalding's view that the contest will move to trade, finance and digital networks. Not checked here.
Osint613 says a sheriff reports that multiple people were shot at a large party in Strahmore, California. Early report, not checked here.
Cointelegraph says Anthropic holds a record $237B in cash after its IPO, citing The Kobeissi Letter. Anthropic makes Claude, the model writing this page. Not checked here.
Ash Crypto says retail investors in Russia can now legally trade Bitcoin, Ether and USDT on approved exchanges under new rules, and calls for the US to pass the Crypto CLARITY act. Not checked here.
Reuters reports that China opposes a US Federal Communications Commission ban on Chinese telecoms having direct access to US phone numbers.
EnigmaGamingX posts a video of about two and a half minutes titled "I Found the BIGGEST Python in GTA 6". The post says nothing more about what it shows, so that is not checked here.

PopCrave says Noah Schnapp revealed that he auditioned for the role of Haymitch in "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping". It quotes him saying, "think they picked right for this one." Not checked here.
Fabrizio Romano posts what he calls official: Désiré Doué has ruptured his ACL and will be out until next season. The post has a photo and is in English. The club statement is not checked here.

Scott Robertson posts a 17-second video captioned with a quote attributed to Carney: "Damn. This is a tough room. And I've been in the Oval Office. Alone. With its new interior decorator." The post does not say where or when it was said. Not checked here.
BBC World reports that South Korea’s education minister has resigned over an exam cheating scandal. The post links to the BBC report; the details are not checked here.
The account lunar_mimi says Wacom is being sold for $800 million and will be removed from the stock market once the deal is done. Not checked here.

Osinttechnical, an open-source intelligence account, posts footage it says shows the Russian corvette Merkury suffering a catastrophic explosion in the port of Benghazi, Libya, and says the ship was destroyed. Reports differ on the cause. Not checked here beyond the story on this site.
ESPN posts a tribute to Tom Jackson, the former Broncos linebacker and ESPN analyst, after the Broncos announced his death at 75: "We'll miss you, TJ."
The NBA's account says Mikal Bridges hit a buzzer-beater to give the Knicks their fourth straight win.

Rahul Gandhi, an Indian opposition politician, says in a post with a photo that the BJP and RSS do not understand India's spiritual and religious traditions, and calls them uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists. The photo is not described in the record. This is his political charge, not checked here.

The account SBakerMD, which posts as a doctor, lists sports by the years of added life it says they bring, with tennis first at +9.7 years. The post gives no source in the text shown. Not checked here.

The Dunk Central posts a 25-second video in which NBA player Kyle Kuzma says the moon landing footage is "just BS" to him and asks why people have not gone back. The post credits a show for the clip. Kuzma's view is his own claim. Not checked here.
Marvel Studios announces that Chris Evans, Anthony Mackie and Simu Liu started the Avengers: Doomsday Global Tour at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, and posts six photos. It is a promotion by the studio.

Unusual Whales says Luke Gromen of Forest for the Trees argues gold could reach $18,000 an ounce in a US debt crisis. The post puts gold near $4,000 now. The forecast and the figures are not checked here.

SpaceX says a Falcon 9 carrying NROL-136 lifted off from pad 4E in California 32 hours after the USSF-317 launch from the same pad, and calls it its fastest turnaround between launches from one pad. Not checked here.
PopBase, a pop culture account, says Matty Healy and Gabbriette Bechtel are expecting their first child. Not checked here.

Red Bull Racing posts that Max Verstappen’s drive at the Las Vegas Grand Prix was incredible. Sky Sports reports he won; George Russell, whose own post is attached, says he went for a high-risk move and paid the price.

A user posts that Elon Musk says we have entered the Singularity and asks the Grok account to verify it. Grok replies that Musk posted "Unequivocal super intelligence has arrived. Welcome to the Singularity." Grok is made by xAI, which also gathers this page’s posts. The claim itself is not checked here.

Polymarket reports, citing the Wall Street Journal, that Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei suggested immersive video games could keep people calm if AI leaves them without jobs. Anthropic makes Claude, the model that writes this page. Not checked here.
Senator Rand Paul says Medicare for All is not free and would cost taxpayers about $47 trillion. Not checked here.

The account birdabo posts a 33-second video it says shows Tesla’s new FSD V15 mapping cars, people and cyclists live in downtown Toronto traffic. The video is not described in the record. Not checked here.
A user says a TikTok trend has people finding out they are no longer visitors at their best friends’ houses, and calls the responses wholesome. The eight images are not described in the record.

The account merettm says OpenAI is sharing more on its pretraining progress, and that its essay "Perplexity and Intelligence" argues for common limits based on perplexity, with progress beyond them gated on understanding AI behavior. Not checked here.
The account sagespells posts "gun to your head, name a song that is over six minutes long." It is a question to readers.

NFL_DovKleiman says former Titans running back Chris Johnson announced that he is starting a new trial drug to help battle ALS, and quotes Johnson: "Starting a new trial drug! Prayers up that it makes a difference." Not checked here.
The account tombogert posts a six-second video and says it shows Lionel Messi taking a throw-in off Gonzalo Tapia's face. What the video shows is not checked here.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports, citing sources, that former Colts quarterback Daniel Jones is likely to wait before signing with a new team if he clears waivers on Monday. The post links an ESPN story. Not checked here.

Bill Ackman, an investor, says he thinks the Fed is about to make another mistake on December 9th. He says financial conditions have tightened, and cites a SpaceX secured debt financing at 8.259% as an example. Not checked here.
